Hidradenitis suppurativa

A small retrospective diode-laser cohort reported clinical improvement, but its procedure targets hair follicles and is not clearly a low-dose PBM protocol. Two cell studies provide mechanistic findings only.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A small retrospective diode-laser cohort reported clinical improvement, but its procedure targets hair follicles and is not clearly a low-dose PBM protocol. Two cell studies provide mechanistic findings only.

Summary of the Evidence

Four publications are grouped under hidradenitis suppurativa: one retrospective 808-nm diode-laser study, two in-vitro PBM studies, and one review. The clinical procedure targets hair follicles and is not clearly a low-dose PBM protocol. The review adds no patient cohort. No animal study was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

The retrospective study included 16 patients treated over two to four sessions. At six months, median disease score fell from 20 to 9, physician global assessment from 3 to 2, and quality-of-life score from 4.5 to 1. Eight of ten people assessed met the HiSCR response definition. Mild pain was reported without severe adverse effects. With no control group and a hair-targeting procedure, this does not establish low-dose PBM efficacy (Özdemir and Tamer 2024).

Animal evidence

No animal experiment was identified in the direct category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

In NCSTN- or PSENEN-related cellular models, 970-nm near-infrared PBM increased metabolism, ATP production, proliferation, or migration. A separate study found that blue visible light at 445 nm and near-infrared light at 970 nm reduced IL1B expression after inflammatory stimulation. These are laboratory findings, not patient replications (Zupin et al. 2020 Ferri et al. 2019).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The clinical report used 808-nm near-infrared diode laser but lacks enough dosimetry for comparison with low-dose PBM. Cell studies used 970-nm light at 30 J/cm² and 0.15 W/cm², or 445-nm blue and 970-nm near-infrared protocols. Laboratory exposure does not define a clinical schedule.

Interpretation

Clinical score changes come from one uncontrolled procedure series. Cell studies describe metabolic and inflammatory responses, not lesion clearance. Patient trials need to define whether light targets follicles, lesions, or both.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for clinical benefit from PBM in hidradenitis suppurativa Very low for short-term outcomes after hair-targeting diode laser treatment
Publications and records4 articles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The only clinical cohort is retrospective and describes a hair-targeting 808-nm diode procedure, not a clearly specified low-dose PBM protocol. Two cell studies report biological responses but cannot show lesion improvement in patients. A controlled study of a defined PBM protocol, compared with sham or standard care and followed for recurrence, would be needed to support a stronger clinical rating.
